purpose: Close a path-injection defect in two web BFF proxies, found while assessing ASVS V1.1.1 and V1.2.2. /api/staff/[...path] and /api/proxy/[...path] concatenated decoded catch-all segments straight into the upstream URL, which fetch() parses again under the WHATWG URL algorithm. A segment containing '?' or '#' moved the rest of the path into a query or fragment, and a segment '%2e%2e' (the raw request '%252e%252e', decoded once by Next.js) is a dot-segment that walks the upstream path. Measured with the real route handlers and fetch mocked: /api/staff forwarded organizations/%2e%2e/users, which its allowlist admits, as /api/staff/users; /api/proxy forwarded %2e%2e/metrics as /metrics, outside the API's /api global prefix, reaching the unauthenticated Prometheus endpoint and /health/detailed that are meant to be reachable only inside the Compose network. Both routes require an authenticated session, so the exposure is to any signed-in user, not to anonymous callers. Five other catch-all proxies were checked and are not exploitable: four admit only a strict identifier charset, and /api/staff/workspaces already encodes each segment.
requiredInvariants: The allowlist, denylist, CSRF, session and header handling of both proxies are unchanged; only how the already-checked path is serialized into the upstream URL changes.

Every segment is percent-encoded on its own before it is joined, so the upstream receives exactly the segments that were checked. A literal '.' or '..' is refused, because encoding leaves it a dot-segment.
An ordinary identifier path is forwarded byte-for-byte as before.
The two source-shape tests that pinned the old targetUrl line are updated to the new line, keeping what they assert: the target is API_BASE_URL/staff/ followed by the allowlisted path.
New test files are wired into the CI-gated web-unit step, not added to the exclusion registry.
The cryptographic inventory is regenerated by scripts/security/discover-cryptography.mjs, never edited by hand; the only change is the scanned-file count and source SHA from the one new file.
No migration, schema, dependency, lockfile or production configuration change.
Merge and CI success are not REG.RU production deployment evidence.
ownerRatificationRequired: Scope authorization. It is the repository's declared source-controlled mechanism, but it is self-declared and requires owner ratification in review before it counts as authorization.
acceptance: Through both proxies, a segment containing '?' or '#' reaches the upstream encoded, with no query or fragment it did not carry.
Through both proxies, a percent-encoded dot-segment no longer changes the upstream path; through /api/proxy the upstream path always stays under the API's /api prefix.
A literal dot-segment is refused before anything is forwarded.
Mutation checks: restoring the raw ${path} concatenation in either route, or removing the dot-segment guard from encodeUpstreamPath, makes the new tests fail; restoring the fix makes them pass again.
node scripts/security/verify-web-unit-coverage.mjs passes, and the exact CI web-unit vitest command passes in full.
